TOPICS: safety instructions, hazard warnings, user responsibilities, device misuse, safety devices, child safety, electrical hazards, burn/scalding risks, mechanical hazards, health hazards, intended use, installation requirements, fire risks, safe distances

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Failure to follow safety instructions can result in death or serious injury. (Page 6)
- Safety is one of the most essential product features at WMF. (Page 6)
- Users must read the User Manual carefully prior to use. (Page 6)
- Do not touch hot machine components. (Page 6)
- Do not use the coffee machine if it is not working properly or is damaged. (Page 6)
- Use the coffee machine only when it is completely assembled. (Page 6)
- Built-in safety devices must never be altered. (Page 7)
- The device can be used by children of age 8 or greater while under continuous supervision. (Page 7)
- Children may not play with the device. (Page 7)
- Cleaning and user maintenance must not be performed by children. (Page 7)
- Despite safety devices, every coffee machine poses potential hazard if incorrectly used. (Page 8)
- Hazard to life due to electrical shock is explicitly warned about. (Page 8)
- Never open the housing, never loosen screws, do not remove housing parts, never use a damaged power cord, avoid damage to the power cord, and do not kink or crush it. (Page 8)
- Burn hazard / scalding hazard: Hot liquid comes out of spouts, adjacent surfaces become hot. (Page 9)
- Do not reach beneath the spouts or touch them immediately after dispensing. (Page 9)
- Always place a suitable cup under the spout before dispensing beverages. (Page 9)
- Risk of injury: Long hair could become caught in the grinder head and drawn into the coffee machine. (Page 9)
- Always protect hair with a hairnet before removing the bean hopper. (Page 9)
- The coffee machine contains moving parts that can cause finger or hand injury. (Page 10)
- Closing the operating panel can cause a crushing hazard. (Page 10)
- Users must always switch off the coffee machine and unplug it before reaching into the grinder or brewing unit. (Page 10)
- Only use products suitable for consumption and with the coffee machine. (Page 10)
- The powder hopper, bean hopper, and manual insert may only be filled with materials for their intended use. (Page 10)
- The milk system cleaner and cleaning tablets are irritants. (Page 11)
- During cleaning, hot cleaning solution and hot water can run out of the combi spout and hot water spout. (Page 11)
- The hot liquids can irritate the skin and pose a burn hazard. (Page 11)
- The drip tray may contain hot liquids. (Page 11)
- Users should never reach under the spouts while cleaning and ensure no one drinks the cleaning solution. (Page 11)
- The WMF 1500 S is designed to dispense beverages made with coffee, milk, and/or powder (such as chocolate or topping). (Page 12)
- The device is intended for industrial and commercial use and should be operated by experts or trained users. (Page 12)
- It can be used in a domestic environment if supervised by trained personnel. (Page 12)
- Misuse of the machine could lead to a risk of injury. (Page 12)
- Fluids can be discharged from the coffee machine if used improperly or if errors occur, creating a slipping hazard. (Page 12)
- The use of the device is subject to this User Manual. (Page 13)
- The WMF 1500 S may only be used for coffee, hot water (beverages, cleaning), or specific types of milk. (Page 13)
- Any necessary on-site preparatory work for electricity, water, and drainage must be arranged by the machine owner/operator. (Page 13)
- WMF Service is neither authorised nor responsible for carrying out any on-site installation work prior to connection. (Page 13)
- The potential equalization terminal is installed by WMF Service if needed. (Page 13)
- The section is titled "2.1 Parts of the coffee machine". (Page 14)

SECTION: 3 Operation (Pages 18-28)

TOPICS: operation safety instructions, switching on/off, milk dispensing, beverage dispensing, steam function, height adjustment, hopper refilling, grounds container, drip tray, display interface, software overview

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Page 18: Burn hazard / scalding hazard: Hot liquid comes out of spouts; do not touch spouts immediately after dispensing; always place a cup under the spout. Health hazard: Only use consumable products; the powder hopper, bean hopper, and manual insert may only be filled with materials for their intended use. Two CAUTION notices instruct to follow the Safety chapter starting on page 6.
- Page 19: The coffee machine is switched on by sliding the operating panel upward and pressing the ON/OFF switch. After switching on, the machine heats up and performs an automatic warm rinsing cycle. The "Ready to operate" display appears when the machine is ready to dispense beverages. Milk can be connected using a suitable milk nozzle on the combi spout. The hose must reach the floor of the milk package and must not be under tension or bent when adjusting the height of the combi spout. The coffee machine can be switched off using the timer.
- Page 20: A CAUTION box warns of a bruising or crushing hazard due to rotating gears and states the milk pump may only be opened by the Service department. The text lists compatible products: WMF milk cooler, WMF Cup&Cool, Easy Milk, and Dynamic Milk (optional). Instructions are provided for inserting the milk nozzle into the combi spout, removing the milk container, and placing it back in the cooler. The beverage is dispensed according to recipe settings, including the dispensing option and milk foam quality. The "Basic Milk" procedure involves inserting the adapter on the milk hose into the connection in the milk container lid. The dispensing options include "Cup volume" (referenced on page 36) and "Start-Stop or metered".
- Page 21: Pressing a beverage button triggers dispensing of the selected beverage. Lit up button = ready to dispense; Unlit button = not ready to dispense / button disabled. Preselection pads (e.g., caffeine-free) define desired settings prior to beverage selection. Special buttons for sizes S, M, and L are optional; S is approx. 25% less than M, L is approx. 25% more than M. Button allocation is detailed on page 41.
- Page 22: Section 3.7 describes hot water dispensing: place a cup under the spout and touch the hot water button. Section 3.8 covers the optional Basic Steam function, which dispenses steam as long as the button is held down. A "Burn hazard / scalding hazard" section warns that hot liquid and steam can cause burns and advises not to reach beneath the spouts or touch them immediately after use. The text states that steam is used to warm beverages and manually foam milk. A CAUTION box instructs the user to follow the Safety chapter starting on page 6.
- Page 23: Use a Cromargan® jug, such as WMF order number 03 9090 0030 or 03 9090 0050. For warm beverages, fill the jug no more than half way and immerse the steam nozzle deeply. Do not overheat milk when foaming, otherwise milk foam volume decreases. A thick creamy milk foam results from rotating the jug in a clockwise direction while pressing the steam button. Residue in the steam outlet tube is rinsed, and the outlet should be wiped with a damp cloth.
- Page 24: The combi spout is height adjustable with a clearance height of 70–175 mm. Hoppers should be filled no more than for one day to maintain product freshness. Foreign objects can damage the grinders and are not covered under warranty. The manual/tablet insert is located in the center of the coffee machine cover. Tablet insert is used for inserting cleaning tablets. Manual insert is used for inserting cleaning tablets, additional coffee types like decaffeinated coffee, and for a coffee trial. An IMPORTANT notice directs users to the Warranty chapter starting on page 97.
- Page 25: The grounds container has capacity for approx. 50 brewing cycles. Beverage dispensing is blocked when the grounds container is removed. Replacing the container without emptying results in overfilling and potential machine damage. The display shows a message when the grounds container needs to be emptied. Instructions for preparing ground coffee using the manual insert are provided, including inserting up to 16 g of ground coffee. A warning states that adding ground coffee or cleaning tablets should only occur after the display message appears.
- Page 26: Grounds disposal through the counter is an optional feature that requires openings in both the grounds container and machine base. Spent coffee grounds are collected in a separate container under the counter. A scalding hazard exists as the drip tray may contain hot liquids; it must be moved carefully and reinserted properly. For machines without a drain connection, the drip tray must be emptied regularly. On machines with a drain connection, the drip tray can be removed for cleaning. If equipped with a drip tray sensor, the machine will indicate on the display when the maximum fill level is reached. After the display message, the user must remove the drip tray carefully, empty it, and reinsert it. Important notes include cleaning the grounds chute daily and following the Safety chapter starting on page 6 and Care starting on page 59.
- Page 27: The section is titled "3.15 Switch off the coffee machine". Users must "Take care to work hygienically" and perform daily cleaning before switching off. Failure to follow the manual invalidates liability for any resultant damage. The ON/OFF switch is located on the right side, behind the operating panel. To switch off, press the ON/OFF switch briefly (approx. 1 second). After switching off, users must disconnect the mains plug and turn off the main water supply tap. Cross-references are provided for the Safety chapter (page 6), Care (page 59), Warranty (page 97), and PIN rights (page 48).
- Page 28: A CAUTION note states that operation safety instructions apply when adjusting beverages and directs users to page 18. The section "4.1 Overview" introduces the "Ready to operate" display. Text notes that the pads and buttons on the display are available depending on the settings and machine model. Specific features like "Barista (coffee strength)" and "Warm rinsing" are listed with their respective page numbers (page 30).

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Failure to follow safety instructions can result in death or serious injury. (Page 6)
- Safety is one of the most essential product features at WMF. (Page 6)
- Users must read the User Manual carefully prior to use. (Page 6)
- Do not touch hot machine components. (Page 6)
- Do not use the coffee machine if it is not working properly or is damaged. (Page 6)
- Use the coffee machine only when it is completely assembled. (Page 6)
- Built-in safety devices must never be altered. (Page 7)
- The device can be used by children of age 8 or greater while under continuous supervision. (Page 7)
- Children may not play with the device. (Page 7)
- Cleaning and user maintenance must not be performed by children. (Page 7)
- Despite safety devices, every coffee machine poses potential hazard if incorrectly used. (Page 8)
- Hazard to life due to electrical shock is explicitly warned about. (Page 8)
- Never open the housing, never loosen screws, do not remove housing parts, never use a damaged power cord, avoid damage to the power cord, and do not kink or crush it. (Page 8)
- Burn hazard / scalding hazard: Hot liquid comes out of spouts, adjacent surfaces become hot. (Page 9)
- Do not reach beneath the spouts or touch them immediately after dispensing. (Page 9)
- Always place a suitable cup under the spout before dispensing beverages. (Page 9)
- Risk of injury: Long hair could become caught in the grinder head and drawn into the coffee machine. (Page 9)
- Always protect hair with a hairnet before removing the bean hopper. (Page 9)
- The coffee machine contains moving parts that can cause finger or hand injury. (Page 10)
- Closing the operating panel can cause a crushing hazard. (Page 10)
- Users must always switch off the coffee machine and unplug it before reaching into the grinder or brewing unit. (Page 10)

sections.summary:
SECTION: 3 Operation (Pages 18-28)

TOPICS: operation safety instructions, switching on/off, milk dispensing, beverage dispensing, steam function, height adjustment, hopper refilling, grounds container, drip tray, display interface, software overview

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Page 18: Burn hazard / scalding hazard: Hot liquid comes out of spouts; do not touch spouts immediately after dispensing; always place a cup under the spout. Health hazard: Only use consumable products; the powder hopper, bean hopper, and manual insert may only be filled with materials for their intended use. Two CAUTION notices instruct to follow the Safety chapter starting on page 6.
- Page 19: The coffee machine is switched on by sliding the operating panel upward and pressing the ON/OFF switch. After switching on, the machine heats up and performs an automatic warm rinsing cycle. The "Ready to operate" display appears when the machine is ready to dispense beverages. Milk can be connected using a suitable milk nozzle on the combi spout. The hose must reach the floor of the milk package and must not be under tension or bent when adjusting the height of the combi spout. The coffee machine can be switched off using the timer.
- Page 20: A CAUTION box warns of a bruising or crushing hazard due to rotating gears and states the milk pump may only be opened by the Service department. The text lists compatible products: WMF milk cooler, WMF Cup&Cool, Easy Milk, and Dynamic Milk (optional). Instructions are provided for inserting the milk nozzle into the combi spout, removing the milk container, and placing it back in the cooler. The beverage is dispensed according to recipe settings, including the dispensing option and milk foam quality. The "Basic Milk" procedure involves inserting the adapter on the milk hose into the connection in the milk container lid. The dispensing options include "Cup volume" (referenced on page 36) and "Start-Stop or metered".
- Page 21: Pressing a beverage button triggers dispensing of the selected beverage. Lit up button = ready to dispense; Unlit button = not ready to dispense / button disabled. Preselection pads (e.g., caffeine-free) define desired settings prior to beverage selection. Special buttons for sizes S, M, and L are optional; S is approx. 25% less than M, L is approx. 25% more than M. Button allocation is detailed on page 41.
- Page 22: Section 3.7 describes hot water dispensing: place a cup under the spout and touch the hot water button. Section 3.8 covers the optional Basic Steam function, which dispenses steam as long as the button is held down. A "Burn hazard / scalding hazard" section warns that hot liquid and steam can cause burns and advises not to reach beneath the spouts or touch them immediately after use. The text states that steam is used to warm beverages and manually foam milk. A CAUTION box instructs the user to follow the Safety chapter starting on page 6.
- Page 23: Use a Cromargan® jug, such as WMF order number 03 9090 0030 or 03 9090 0050. For warm beverages, fill the jug no more than half way and immerse the steam nozzle deeply. Do not overheat milk when foaming, otherwise milk foam volume decreases. A thick creamy milk foam results from rotating the jug in a clockwise direction while pressing the steam button. Residue in the steam outlet tube is rinsed, and the outlet should be wiped with a damp cloth.
- Page 24: The combi spout is height adjustable with a clearance height of 70–175 mm. Hoppers should be filled no more than for one day to maintain product freshness. Foreign objects can damage the grinders and are not covered under warranty. The manual/tablet insert is located in the center of the coffee machine cover. Tablet insert is used for inserting cleaning tablets. Manual insert is used for inserting cleaning tablets, additional coffee types like decaffeinated coffee, and for a coffee trial. An IMPORTANT notice directs users to the Warranty chapter starting on page 97.
- Page 25: The grounds container has capacity for approx. 50 brewing cycles. Beverage dispensing is blocked when the grounds container is removed. Replacing the container without emptying results in overfilling and potential machine damage. The display shows a message when the grounds container needs to be emptied. Instructions for preparing ground coffee using the manual insert are provided, including inserting up to 16 g of ground coffee. A warning states that adding ground coffee or cleaning tablets should only occur after the display message appears.
- Page 26: Grounds disposal through the counter is an optional feature that requires openings in both the grounds container and machine base. Spent coffee grounds are collected in a separate container under the counter. A scalding hazard exists as the drip tray may contain hot liquids; it must be moved carefully and reinserted properly. For machines without a drain connection, the drip tray must be emptied regularly. On machines with a drain connection, the drip tray can be removed for cleaning. If equipped with a drip tray sensor, the machine will indicate on the display when the maximum fill level is reached. After the display message, the user must remove the drip tray carefully, empty it, and reinsert it. Important notes include cleaning the grounds chute daily and following the Safety chapter starting on page 6 and Care starting on page 59.
- Page 27: The section is titled "3.15 Switch off the coffee machine". Users must "Take care to work hygienically" and perform daily cleaning before switching off. Failure to follow the manual invalidates liability for any resultant damage. The ON/OFF switch is located on the right side, behind the operating panel. To switch off, press the ON/OFF switch briefly (approx. 1 second). After switching off, users must disconnect the mains plug and turn off the main water supply tap. Cross-references are provided for the Safety chapter (page 6), Care (page 59), Warranty (page 97), and PIN rights (page 48).
- Page 28: A CAUTION note states that operation safety instructions apply when adjusting beverages and directs users to page 18. The section "4.1 Overview" introduces the "Ready to operate" display. Text notes that the pads and buttons on the display are available depending on the settings and machine model. Specific features like "Barista (coffee strength)" and "Warm rinsing" are listed with their respective page numbers (page 30).

The burn hazard section warns that hot liquid can emerge from spouts during beverage dispensing, advising users not to touch the spouts immediately after use and to place a cup underneath. The health hazard section specifies that only products suitable for consumption should be used with the coffee machine, and that components like the powder hopper and bean hopper must only be filled with intended materials. - Health hazard: Only use consumable products; the powder hopper, bean hopper, and manual insert may only be filled with materials for their intended use.
- Two CAUTION notices instruct to follow the Safety chapter starting on page 6.

pages.ocr_text: Cup volume, multiple brewing, and dispensing option Cup volume Set the desired cup volume. The recipe is adjusted accordingly. $100\%$  indicates the previously saved value. Cup volume S-M-L The recipes for the sizes S and L are generated. M is as set. Default value: $S = 25\%$  less than the setting. $L = 25\%$  more than the setting. The S-M-L function can be activated in the operating options. The cup volume can also be set to a different general level for all beverages using the operating options. For individual beverages that deviate from the standard, the S-M-L amounts can be changed under Cup volume. Each size can also be individually set to active or inactive. Inactive means that the size no longer appears as a selection for the individual beverage. Multiple brewing cycles The beverage is brewed several times, as set. Up to 12 times the set amount can be dispensed with one push of a button. Available for beverages with coffee and with milk mixtures, as well as for hot water with the "metered" dispensing option. pages.ocr_text: Dynamic Milk foam quality levels Coffee machines with Dynamic Milk can use different milk foam quality levels for each beverages. It is possible to combine several milk foam quality levels in one beverage. Firm Firm milk foam. Recommended for cappuccinos with a brown edge and for beverages where the appearance of the milk foam is important, along with balanced milk flavor. Soft Very fine milk foam. Recommended for cappuccinos with balanced and very distinct milk flavor. Optimal blending of coffee and milk. Creamy Milk foam with a shiny surface. Recommended for milk beverages with balanced milk flavor and a good blend of coffee and milk. Fluffy Fluffy, light milk foam with a somewhat coarser bubble structure and balanced milk flavor. Coffee quality The quality levels influence the coffee brewing. The higher the quality level, the more intensive the release of the flavour and aromatic substances in the coffee. Quality levels Instructions: If very finely ground coffee is used with a small amount of brewing water, a high quality level can cause a brewing water flow error.
pages.summary:
This page from the User Manual WMF 1500 S (page 39) details two key features of coffee machines: Dynamic Milk foam quality levels and Coffee quality settings. It describes four milk foam types—Firm, Soft, Creamy, and Fluffy—each with specific characteristics and recommended beverage applications. The page also outlines a seven-level coffee quality system where higher levels intensify flavor release, with detailed instructions for each level and a warning about potential brewing water flow errors with very finely ground coffee. A small diagram illustrates the coffee brewing process.

**Text Evidence:**
- Coffee machines with Dynamic Milk can use different milk foam quality levels for each beverage.
- It is possible to combine several milk foam quality levels in one beverage.
- Firm milk foam is recommended for cappuccinos with a brown edge and for beverages where the appearance of the milk foam is important.
- Soft milk foam is recommended for cappuccinos with balanced and very distinct milk flavor.
- Creamy milk foam has a shiny surface and is recommended for milk beverages with balanced milk flavor.
- Fluffy milk foam is light with a somewhat coarser bubble structure.
- The higher the coffee quality level, the more intensive the release of flavour and aromatic substances.
- A high quality level can cause a brewing water flow error if very finely ground coffee is used with a small amount of brewing water.

- Error message options are Text and Symbol; default is Text (Page 45)
- The PostSelection feature requests coffee type and amount after selection and allows modification of coffee types and sizes (S-M-L) (Page 45)
- Beverage dispensing can be interrupted by pressing the beverage button again when Cancel beverage is active (Page 45)

- The Timer option displays a weekly overview of all switch-on and switch-off times (Page 46)
- The Service option provides contact data for WMF Service and the coffee machine's serial number (Page 46)
- The Care option displays records of the last cleaning and care actions (Page 46)
- The Water filter and descaling option shows the remaining capacity of the water filter and the next decalcification time (Page 46)
- The Journal option contains records of events and faults during operation and cleaning (Page 46)

pages.summary:
This page (Page 46) from the WMF 1500 S User Manual details the "Information" menu, which provides access to various system functions. The menu includes options for viewing the last brewing cycle, managing the weekly timer, accessing service contact data and the serial number, checking care actions, monitoring water filter and descaling status, reviewing operational journals, and displaying or exporting the user manual. A visual flowchart on the right illustrates the hierarchical navigation path through these menu items.

**Text Evidence:**
- The info menu has selection options including Last brewing cycle, Timer, Service, Care, Water filter and descaling, Journal, and User Manual.
- The Last brewing cycle option shows information about the most recent brew.
- The Timer option displays a weekly overview of all switch-on and switch-off times.
- The Service option provides contact data for WMF Service and the coffee machine's serial number.
- The Care option displays records of the last cleaning and care actions.
- The Water filter and descaling option shows the remaining capacity of the water filter and the next decalcification time.
- The Journal option contains records of events and faults during operation and cleaning.
- The User Manual can be displayed on the screen or exported via USB.

**Visual Evidence:**
<figure_summary>Figure: Navigation Flow - This diagram shows the path from the main home icon to the 'Info' menu, then down a list of six options: Last brewing cycle, Timer, Service, Care, Filter/descaling, and Journal, ending with User Manual. pages.summary:
This page (Page 48) from the User Manual WMF 1500 S details the PIN rights system, explaining that one PIN can be assigned for each of three hierarchical areas: Cleaning, Settings, and Accounting. The hierarchy means a higher-level PIN (e.g., Settings) grants access to all lower-level functions (e.g., Cleaning), but not to functions in other independent branches (e.g., Accounting). The document lists the specific access permissions for each PIN level, such as Care, Beverages, and System, and includes a diagram illustrating the hierarchical flow from Settings to Cleaning and Accounting.

- If a PIN has been assigned, no access will be granted without it.

It includes two prominent warning sections: a "Burn hazard" cautioning users about hot surfaces and a "CAUTION" box directing them to the Safety chapter starting on page 6. **Text Evidence:**
- A "Burn hazard" warning states the brewing unit can be hot after switching off and must be allowed to cool before cleaning.

sections.summary:
SECTION: 10 Safety and warranty (Pages 93-98)

TOPICS: safety instructions, warranty conditions, regulatory compliance, maintenance responsibilities, technical specifications

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Failure to observe the manual's requirements voids the warranty for any resulting damage (Page 93)
- The installation location must be dry and protected against water spray (Page 93)
- The coffee machine should not be used outdoors (Page 93)
- The machine must be placed on a water-resistant and heatproof base (Page 93)
- Foreign objects can damage the grinders and are not covered under warranty (Page 93)
- A WMF water filter must be fitted for drinking water with carbonate hardness in excess of 5 °dKH to prevent damage (Page 94)
- For insurance reasons, the main water supply tap must be turned off and the mains switch or plug must be disconnected at the end of operation (Page 94)
- Damage prevention measures include the installation of a suitable water monitor and smoke alarms (Page 94)
- After being shut off for several days, the cleaning program should be run at least twice before reusing the machine (Page 94)
- The device fulfills the German Food and Feed Code (LFGB), Regulation on Commodities (BedGgstV), EU regulation No. 10/2011, and EU regulation No. 1935/2004 (Page 95)
- The device complies with directives MD (MR) 2006/42/EC (EG), Directive 2004/108/EC (EMC), Directive 2011/65/EC (ROHS), and Directive 2002/96/EC (WEEE) (Page 95)
- The device bears the CE mark and has a declaration of conformity included (Page 95)
- Any modifications not approved by WMF will invalidate the declaration (Page 95)
- The device is subject to the WEEE/EU directive and cannot be disposed of as domestic waste (Page 95)
- Requirements traceability and Good Manufacturing Practice are ensured per EC regulations No. 1935/2004 and 2023/2006 (Page 95)
- For disposal, contact WMF Service; address is on page 85 (Page 95)
- The operator must ensure regular maintenance by WMF Service technicians or other authorized persons (Page 96)
- Access to the service area is restricted to persons with knowledge and practical experience regarding safety and hygiene (Page 96)
- In self-service applications, only staff instructed in operation should supervise the machine (Page 96)
- Electrical equipment must be in a fit state, referencing BGV A3 (German Accident Prevention Association) (Page 96)
- Regular checks of safety valves and pressure containers are essential for operating safety (Page 96)
- Machine cleaning must use only the WMF special cleaning agent (tablets for coffee machine, liquid for milk system) (Page 96)
- Manufacturer's specifications for maintenance cycles and frequency must be observed (Page 96)
- Warranty claims may be voided if the requirements of this User Manual are not followed (Page 97)
- No warranty is provided for damage from natural wear and tear, including seals, mixers, and brewing units (Page 97)
- No warranty is provided for malfunctions due to weather, scale build-up, chemical, physical, electrochemical, or electrical effects (Page 97)
- No warranty is provided if a water filter is not fitted when required, or if malfunctions result from failure to follow handling, maintenance, and care instructions (Page 97)
- No warranty is provided for faults caused by using original WMF spare parts incorrectly, third-party assembly, or faulty/negligent treatment (Page 97)
- No warranty is provided for consequences of improper modifications, repairs, or reconditioning without consent (Page 97)
- The document is titled "Appendix: Technical data" and specifies it is from the "User Manual WMF 1500 S" (Page 98)
- The main table lists detailed technical specifications for a coffee machine (Page 98)
- Footnotes clarify that hopper capacities depend on bean size and powder usage, and that the sound pressure level is measured under specific conditions (Page 98)
- A final statement reiterates the company's right to make technical modifications (Page 98)

Access to the service area is permitted only for persons with knowledge and practical experience with the device, especially regarding safety and hygiene. pages.ocr_text: These specifications for the electrical connection and the standards quoted apply for connecting the coffee machine in EU countries. It may be necessary to also observe additional country-specific regulations. Outside the EU countries acceptance of the standards quoted is to be checked by the legal entity or natural person who wishes to use the coffee machine. The local power supply must be constructed according to the currently valid IEC 364 (DIN VDE 0100). An isolated ground outlet or a country-specific single-phase outlet for single-phase connection, or a 5-pole CEE / CEKON socket per EN 60309 or a country-specific multi-pole socket for a three-phase connection, must be available near the machine. The sockets are part of the customer's on-site installation. The mains cable must not come into contact with hot surfaces. If the mains cable for this device is damaged then it must be replaced by our service personnel or a similarly qualified person, in order to prevent hazards. In order to avoid possible faults from arising on our shielded data lines due to potential equalisation currents between the devices, an additional potential equalisation unit should be planned for devices connected to the vending system. (See EN 60309)
